top.headline: When the US Military Adopted AI Targeting, Civilian Deaths Doubled in Somalia
top.blurb: Airwars data analyzed by The Intercept shows strikes in Somalia nearly tripled and civilian casualties more than tripled in the two years after the Pentagon's Project Maven targeting AI arrived, with no evidence the system made strikes more accurate. A Somali integration lead is quoted calling the theater "more of a free-for-all," and the piece traces Maven's computer vision — now run by Palantir — through a botched 2019 raid in Syria to a November strike that killed at least 12 civilians, including eight children.

top.headline: A Federal Women's Prison Became a 'Rape Club.' Reporters Found Abuse at Most of the Other 26, Too.
top.blurb: Five years after the FCI Dublin scandal, a ProPublica/Marshall Project investigation found more than 185 cases of staff sexual abuse since 2021 at 16 of the 27 federal prisons holding women, involving 96 officers — yet only 19 have been arrested or convicted. Congress never funded the promised oversight office, and one accused officer at a Texas prison, named by 18 women, was still working as of this month.

top.headline: Trump's Pick to Police Intelligence Lawyers Calls a $1 Million Pardon Bribe a 'Complicated Legal Question'
top.blurb: Asked at his confirmation hearing whether a president could legally accept $1 million in exchange for a pardon, ODNI general-counsel nominee Gary Lawkowski said bribery's interaction with presidential immunity was unsettled law — prompting Sen. Mark Warner to warn that "I was just the lawyer" is becoming a default answer. Lawkowski helped shape the memo directing federal law enforcement to target "antifa," but declined to detail his role, citing attorney-client privilege.

top.headline: Bengaluru's Tunnel Road Is DK Shivakumar's 'Lasting Legacy.' It's Frozen in Court, Over Budget, and Built on a Rushed Report.
top.blurb: Newslaundry found the Chief Minister's signature twin-tunnel project frozen by a High Court order, with Adani's winning bid running Rs 4,600 crore over estimate and a per-kilometre cost nearly double the Metro's — while its Detailed Project Report was finished in three months against a typical nine to twelve, cited locations in the wrong state, and drew a Rs 15 lakh fine for the consultants. The tunnels are car-only and would likely toll Rs 640 a round trip, even as parallel Metro and suburban-rail lines meant for everyone else remain stalled and underfunded.

top.headline: In Mohan Yadav's Ujjain, Journalists Who Criticised Him Say They Were Targeted Until They Left
top.blurb: Newslaundry spoke to reporters in Madhya Pradesh CM Mohan Yadav's home turf who describe a pattern of pressure, harassment and professional isolation after publishing critical coverage, pushing several out of the city altogether. The piece documents how local administration and police allegedly worked in tandem to squeeze out dissenting press rather than through any single dramatic crackdown.

top.headline: Supreme Court Rejects ED's Bid to Undo Azam Khan's Bail, Even as It Insists the Case Against Him Stands
top.blurb: The Supreme Court dismissed the Enforcement Directorate's appeal against the Allahabad High Court's finding that Azam Khan's arrest — timed to the hour after his release in another case, without written grounds — looked "motivated and mala fide," though it clarified those findings won't bind the final verdict. The ED maintains a video shows Khan being handed the arrest grounds and refusing them; his lawyers call the whole case a vendetta to keep him jailed through UP's coming election.

top.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin Hold an Unprecedented Three-Way Summit in China — and Agree on Little Beyond Meeting
top.blurb: The leaders of the world's three major nuclear powers held bilateral talks followed by a first-of-its-kind trilateral sit-down at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, with Trump pushing nuclear arms control and both Ukraine and Iran on the table. Analysts expect no breakthrough — Russia wants sanctions relief and cover for Ukraine, China wants no interference in its own ambitions, and Trump, weakened after the midterms, wants a symbolic win he can sell at home.

top.headline: Bangladesh Deploys Paramilitary Troops as Bomb Blasts and Arson Spread Over Talk of Sheikh Hasina's Return
top.blurb: Police recorded at least 70 crude bomb blasts and 57 arson attacks across 28 districts in ten days, with more than 520 arrests, after Dhaka said it had cleared the legal path to seek the ousted premier's extradition from India and her banned Awami League called a nationwide strike. Hasina's supporters have also set fire to more than 37 branches of Grameen Bank, founded by Muhammad Yunus, who led the interim government that replaced her.

top.headline: Bumrah Rips Through New Zealand's Top Order — Then Nicholls and Phillips Rescue Them With a 173-Run Stand
top.blurb: New Zealand slumped to 70/5 at the Basin Reserve as Jasprit Bumrah took three wickets either side of lunch on the opening day of the first Test, before Henry Nicholls (113 not out, his fifth Basin Reserve century) and Glenn Phillips (94 not out) added 173 together to leave New Zealand 243/5 at the close. India's coach conceded his bowlers should have targeted Phillips's stumps more and that a dropped catch off Nicholls cost them a key opening.

top.headline: Litton's Record Glovework Can't Stop South Africa Piling Up 557 — Now Bangladesh Must Survive a Final Day
top.blurb: South Africa were bowled out for 557 in Johannesburg, a 157-run first-innings lead built on Ryan Rickelton's century and lower-order runs from Kagiso Rabada and a recalled Temba Bavuma, even as wicketkeeper Litton Das set a record for dismissals in a single Test innings. Bangladesh limped to 100/5 in reply, with centurion Towhid Hridoy among the wickets, leaving them 57 runs behind with five wickets in hand heading into the final day.

top.headline: 'I Play Rocky' Review: A Stallone Biopic With None of the Darkness, All of the Persistence
top.blurb: Peter Farrelly's I Play Rocky dramatizes a struggling Sylvester Stallone refusing to let any other actor play the hero of the script he wrote, with Anthony Ippolito's impression of Stallone praised as uncannily accurate. Scroll's review calls it a crowd-pleasing, feel-good salute to persistence and to Hollywood's old willingness to bet on untested talent, even as its 128-minute runtime spends as much affection on the industry as on Stallone's own ordeal.

bengal.headline: As Attacks on Bengal's Christians Mount, BJP's State Chief Warns Missionary Schools Without Naming One
bengal.blurb: BJP Bengal chief Samik Bhattacharya accused Christian schools of forced conversions and anti-India activity without naming any institution or offering evidence, drawing a joint rebuttal from Christian bodies who counter that roughly 50 attacks on prayer meetings over four months have gone largely unpunished, while a bishop asked the chief minister to guarantee a safe Christmas.

bengal.headline: Suvendu Adhikari Promises Tea Garden Workers Land Rights and Permanent Houses on His Third Alipurduar Visit
bengal.blurb: At an Adivasi event in Alipurduar, the chief minister announced land pattas and permanent housing for tea garden workers, job reservations for Adivasis, and a crackdown on fraudulent Scheduled Tribe certificates, while ordering a reopened probe into an attack on a Malda MP.

travel.headline: Mapping Every Jaguar Corridor From Mexico to Argentina to Find Out Which Ones Are Breaking
travel.blurb: Tracking 172 GPS-collared jaguars across eight countries, researchers mapped 307 core habitat areas and 176 corridors connecting them, finding the cat has already vanished from El Salvador and likely Uruguay as soybean farms and cattle pasture sever populations from one another.

happy.headline: A Sketch Hidden for 60 Years Shows an Artist Drawing His Lifelong Muse One Last Time, Days After Her Death
happy.blurb: Discovered in family papers while curators prepared a Tate Britain show, a pencil-and-biro drawing shows Bloomsbury Group painter Duncan Grant sketching Vanessa Bell as she lay dying in 1961 — decades after their complicated, art-bound partnership produced a daughter whose true father she kept secret until adulthood. Charleston's head of collections says Grant got "remarkably close, but apparently not quite close enough," a small imperfection that makes the drawing feel like it was made by hand and grief rather than skill alone.

tech_top.headline: Anthropic's IPO Prices at $83 a Share, the Largest Offering on Record
tech_top.blurb: Anthropic priced its IPO above its $70-78 range, raising about $81.3 billion at a $1.5 trillion valuation and topping SpaceX as the largest offering ever — with Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia and other chipmakers buying $26 billion of non-voting shares alongside the public float. Shares begin trading Thursday under ticker ANT, arriving amid jitters over Nvidia's leadership crisis and AI-stock volatility.
tech_top.pm_note: Pricing above range while buyers accept non-voting shares tells you demand is strong enough that Anthropic didn't need to trade away governance for capital — a signal of negotiating leverage every PM watching vendor or investor term sheets should recognize.

tech_top.headline: Nadella: Much of the World's Critical Infrastructure Is 'Unpatchable,' and AI Is Making That Dangerous
tech_top.blurb: At the DealBook Summit, the Microsoft CEO said newly internet-connected systems like data-center chillers and HVAC firmware often can't be patched at all, even as AI tools find exploitable bugs faster than teams can safely test fixes. He described this week's Outlook outage as a "latent bug" meeting a "perfect storm," with patches now needing to reach production almost instantly because they're being exploited in the wild.
tech_top.pm_note: This is a hardware generation gap colliding with a software-speed problem: devices built with no patch path at all are now facing attackers that move at AI speed, which is a design failure no amount of faster incident response can fully compensate for.

tech_more.headline: Intel Signs Its First Outside Customer for Advanced 18A Chips
tech_more.blurb: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan confirmed an unnamed company has signed on for the 18A-P process, Intel's first marquee outside foundry customer after years of trying to compete with TSMC, though the stock remains down more than 50% since a disappointing September revenue warning.

tech_more.headline: Palo Alto Networks Buys AI Startup Applied Compute for $4.5 Billion, Beats Earnings
tech_more.blurb: Palo Alto's all-stock acquisition of Applied Compute, which helps businesses run and customize open-weight AI models, came alongside a strong earnings beat and raised guidance, with CEO Nikesh Arora predicting the AI-security push "could be bigger than what we do" today.

tech_101.text: Stock that shares in a company's profits but carries no say in how it's run. Chipmakers and cloud giants buying $26 billion of Anthropic's IPO this way got exposure to its upside without any claim on its governance — a sign of how much leverage a hot IPO can retain over even its biggest buyers.

A company that pays a chipmaker to manufacture chips it designed itself, rather than buying chips designed in-house. Intel has spent years trying to build this business to compete with TSMC; landing an unnamed customer for its advanced 18A-P process is the first real evidence it can.

science.headline: A Battery Catalyst Made From Vitamin B12 Just Survived 250 Charge Cycles
science.blurb: University of Córdoba chemists bonded vitamin B12 to carbon nanotubes to build the first rechargeable zinc-air battery catalyzed by the vitamin, anchoring it so it survives the water-based electrolyte that normally dissolves it. The cobalt at B12's core drives both the discharge and recharge reactions, a dual role needed for a rechargeable design and a step toward cheaper alternatives to lithium-ion for storing solar and wind power.

science.headline: NASA Pushed Mars Helicopter Blades Past the Speed of Sound Without Them Breaking
science.blurb: JPL engineers spun experimental rotor blades to Mach 1.08 in a chamber simulating Mars's thin atmosphere, well past the limits that kept the Ingenuity helicopter's blades at a cautious 2,700 RPM across its 72 flights. The result, feeding into the SkyFall helicopter mission due in 2028, could let future Mars rotorcraft carry heavier instruments and fly farther, since thin air forces rotors to spin far faster than on Earth to generate the same lift.

science.headline: Homo Erectus Was Still Living in Dense Chinese Rainforest 184,000 Years Ago, Fossil Teeth Show
science.blurb: Eight teeth from two Guangxi caves, dated by five independent methods, are the youngest confirmed Homo erectus fossils in mainland China and show the species thrived in tropical rainforest long thought survivable only by Homo sapiens. Chemical traces suggest some individuals ranged widely through forested terrain as children, complicating the assumption that rainforests were a dead end for every human lineage except our own.

philosophy.headline: Habermas Built a Theory of Democracy on Staying Open to Persuasion. Did He Actually Practice It?
philosophy.blurb: Emilie Prattico, once his student, traces how Jürgen Habermas revised his own theory over decades: conceding that the bourgeois "public sphere" he idealized had excluded women, and abandoning his earlier claim that truth is simply what people would agree to under fair conditions. In his later work he warned that social media splinters the public into self-enclosed groups, calling a shared, inclusive public sphere a "constitutional imperative" rather than an optional nice-to-have.

philosophy.headline: A Finance Academic's Diagnosis for Ailing Democracies: It Wasn't Bad Luck, It Was Policy
philosophy.blurb: Les Coleman argues that neoliberal reforms dating to Reagan and Thatcher systematically weakened democratic institutions, correlating with higher government debt, slower growth and doubled household debt across OECD countries while wealth concentration let elites shape politics directly. His fixes range from higher politician pay and democracy vouchers to a progressive death tax and an independent economic-crime police unit modeled on Singapore's.

philosophy_101.text: Habermas's name for the shared space where citizens reason together and hold power accountable through open debate. He later conceded its classic 18th-century version quietly excluded women, and warned that social media is now splintering it into self-enclosed groups that no longer argue from shared facts.

An economics framework linking how an industry or system is structured, to how its participants behave, to what outcomes result. Coleman uses it to argue that deregulation-era policy choices structurally produced today's debt and inequality, rather than those outcomes arriving by chance.
